relevance_reason: This paper first describes the disorder: a consanguineous family with cortical malformation caused by a homozygous DMRTA2 frameshift variant.

findings.statement: Urquhart et al. (2016) reported a consanguineous family with 3 affected sibs who had a severe prenatal neurodevelopmental disorder. Features included fronto-parietal pachygyria, agenesis of the corpus callosum, and progressive severe microcephaly.
quotes: A consanguineous family was ascertained with three siblings affected by a severe prenatal neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by fronto-parietal pachygyria, agenesis of the corpus callosum and progressive severe microcephaly.

findings.statement: In the 3 affected sibs of a consanguineous family with CDCBM17, Urquhart et al. (2016) used autozygosity mapping and exome sequencing to identify a novel homozygous 1-bp deletion in the DMRTA2 gene (c.1197delT). The deletion was predicted to cause a frameshift (p.Pro400LeufsTer33). The authors stated that data from murine and zebrafish knockout models were consistent with the variant being responsible for the cortical phenotype. They suggested that loss of function of DMRTA2 leads to a novel disorder of cortical development.
quotes: Autozygosity mapping and exome sequencing identified a homozygous novel single base pair deletion, c.1197delT in DMRTA2, predicted to result in a frameshift variant p.(Pro400Leufs*33).
Data from murine and zebrafish knockout models are consistent with the variant of DMTRA2 (DMRT5) as responsible for the cortical brain phenotype.
Our study suggests that loss of function of DMRTA2 leads to a novel disorder of cortical development.
